claims.quote: STXBP1 mutations are a leading genetic cause of neurodevelopmental disorders.
Of these, 24 had developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE), while 4 (Patients 11, 13, 23, and 27) had developmental delay without seizures.
The most common seizures were focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures (FBTCS), generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS), and epileptic spasms (ES).
The most common seizures were focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures (FBTCS), generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS), and epileptic spasms (ES).
The most common seizures were focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures (FBTCS), generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS), and epileptic spasms (ES).
Among the cohort of 28 patients, 27 individuals (96.4%) exhibited developmental delays.
Of these, 14 patients demonstrated severely impaired intellectual functioning.
Seizure control was achieved in 14 patients and seven patients have had drug-resistant epilepsy.
Regrettably, 3 patients succumbed to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP).
The severity of phenotypes in patients with STXBP1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (STXBP1-DEE) varied from drug-responsive seizures to refractory epilepsy.
